children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar in early trade, but may strengthen amid risk-on sentiment driven by Wall Street's rally overnight. "Risk appetite returned with a vengeance after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, triggering a sharp rebound across battered AI and technology stocks," StoneX's Matt Simpson says in commentary. Although worries over artificial-intelligence valuations, elevated interest rates and slowing economic growth haven't disappeared, there's an improved risk environment, the senior market analyst adds. The U.S. dollar is flat at 1,340.96 won and is little changed at 1.2913 Singapore dollars, while the Australian dollar is steady at US$0.6624, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
